content:
mira: Heads-up — we pushed the soft-throttle smoothing change to 10% of traffic in APAC canary ~2m ago and an enterprise customer reported elevated 429s and timeouts. Seeing a spike in support tickets. Anyone watching?

alex: on it. which policy did we change exactly? policy name and config please.

mira: policy = rate.soft_smoothing.v3, intended change: smoother window from 5s -> 15s and soft_limit from 120rps -> 160rps. burst_max left at 250.

raj: hmm that increase should reduce short-tail 429s, not cause more. do you have request ids or examples?

mira: pasted one request id from the customer email: rid=01G3B8Y2XQ. Logs show 429s around 16:42 UTC. attaching short log snippet:```
[2026-03-17T16:42:12Z] rid=01G3B8Y2XQ user=acme-corp status=429 reason=soft_throttle active=160 rps burst=250 window=15s
[2026-03-17T16:42:13Z] rid=01G3B8Y2XQ kv_cache_hit=false latency_ms=214
```

alex: curious — the log shows active=160 rps which equals the new soft_limit, so the smoothing may be misclassifying bursts as sustained. can you run the internal ratepolicy debug endpoint and paste the live counters?

mira: running now: `curl -u :$TOKEN https://internal.redwood/api/ratepolicy/soft_smoothing.v3/debug?region=apac`

mira: output (trimmed):```
window=15s token_count=160 token_rate=12.0 burst_tokens=250 edge_queue=34 smoothing_factor=0.2
recent_peaks=[180,190,170,200,210]
```

raj: recent_peaks shows short spikes > burst_tokens, so token bucket is draining and clients get 429s when bursts overlap smoothing threshold. The smoothing_factor 0.2 might be too aggressive given telemetry.

sre-oncall: we should stop the canary and roll back the smoothing change while we diagnose. propose: scale canary back to 0% in the router and revert policy to rate.soft_smoothing.v2 (15s window with smoothing_factor 0.35). rollback window 5m.

mira: agree. can someone initiate the rollback? i'll notify the customer.

alex: @deploy-bot can you revert rate.soft_smoothing.v3 in apac canary to previous config? include reason: customer 429s.

deploy-bot: Received rollback request from alex. Starting revert: rate.soft_smoothing.v3 -> rate.soft_smoothing.v2 in region=apac. ETA ~2m.

billing: quick note — this change touched soft limits, might affect short-term billing for heavy customers. alerting billing ops to watch anomalies.

laila: copying runbook step for emergency rollback: `POST /internal/canary/control` body `{ "policy":"rate.soft_smoothing.v3", "action":"set_percent", "percent":0 }` — ran it once for verification.

deploy-bot: Revert complete. Canary scaled to 0% and active policy restored to rate.soft_smoothing.v2. Change id=chg-20260317-91.

mira: thanks all. i told the customer we rolled back and asked for any more request ids. we'll reopen if we see repeat after further tuning.

raj: follow-ups: we'll run a short A/B test with instrumented clients to capture burst shapes, tweak smoothing_factor to 0.28, and re-run canary at 5% with tighter observability. I'll create an RFC and link.

alex: perfect. post the RFC link here when ready and let's coordinate a preflight with eng-runtime. :white_check_mark: 

mira: closing loop with customer — they confirmed errors subsided after rollback. leaving this thread open until RFC posted. 

sre-oncall: marking incident as mitigated. adding notes to the canary playbook about verifying `recent_peaks` and running `token_bucket_snapshot` before rollout.

mira: thanks everyone :pray:
